primitives.verbatim_quote: - In 2014, 5 continents were represented: Europe (UEFA, 13 teams), South America (CONMEBOL, 6 teams), Africa (CAF, 5 teams), North and Central America (CONCACAF, 4 teams), and Asia (AFC, 4 teams).
primitives.assumptions: Equal probability of any team being assigned to any group.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No known breakdown regime; assumes fixed continental quotas.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a constrained allocation problem in combinatorial design, where continental quotas act as hard constraints on the assignment of teams to groups. This isomorphic framework applies to GSI for modeling balanced tournament brackets and to GSE for scheduling resource-constrained tasks.
layer2.telemetry: Measures the degree of continental imbalance in group compositions, such as the variance in the number of European teams per group.

primitives.name: Group Stage Structure
primitives.verbatim_quote: Group stage: the 32 finalists are divided into 8 groups of 4, labeled A through H.
primitives.assumptions: Fixed group size of 4 teams across all 8 groups.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No breakdown; assumes a rigid 8x4 matrix.

layer2.mapping: Represents a fixed-size partitioning kernel, analogous to GSI's clustering algorithms for grouping similar entities into disjoint sets, and to GSE's task scheduling where resources are allocated to fixed-capacity bins.
layer2.telemetry: Tracks the consistency of group composition over multiple tournaments, flagging deviations from the 8x4 structure.

primitives.name: Geographic Separation Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Geographic separation: Teams from the same continent cannot be drawn into the same group.
primitives.assumptions: Strict continental segregation within each group.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violated when two teams from the same continent end up in the same group.

layer2.mapping: Encodes a hard exclusion rule, similar to GSI's disjunctive feature engineering and GSE's collision avoidance protocols in multi-agent pathfinding.
layer2.telemetry: Logs the frequency of continental violations during draws, serving as a direct performance metric.

primitives.name: European Exception
primitives.verbatim_quote: Exception: European teams, since there are more than 8 of them—a maximum of 2 European teams per group is allowed.
primitives.assumptions: Europe has at least 9 participating teams, creating a ceiling on intra-continental pairs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the European quota exceeds 2 teams per group, causing continental overlap.

layer2.mapping: Introduces a soft upper-bound constraint, mirroring GSI's threshold-based anomaly detection and GSE's capacity-limiting state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Records instances where the European cap is exceeded, indicating a structural flaw.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core failure mode is uneven probability distribution due to sequential pot-based drawing without accounting for continental carryover effects. This leads to some continental combinations being systematically more likely than others, violating the principle of equal likelihood for all possible group compositions. The "tractability" mentioned is a red herring; the real issue is the lack of a uniform measure over the space of feasible draws. The "high-ranked teams" bias arises because early-picked pots disproportionately influence later picks, creating a feedback loop. Our proposed method uses a pre-computed list of admissible continental configurations, sampled uniformly, which eliminates this bias by decoupling the continental choice from the team selection.
